raw_response:
I am 64 years old and I have farmed this 4.1 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. I only went to primary school, but I know this land better than any book. I grow wheat in winter and maize in summer — that is what everyone here does, and I am not changing it. I watch my neighbors. If Old Zhang across the lane uses a certain amount and his field looks good, I do the same. Change is risky when you are alone and every yuan matters.

For my wheat this year: I will plant the improved variety I have used for three years now. I saw my neighbor get a good harvest with it, so I switched and it worked for me too. I sow about 15 kg of seed per mu. For fertilizer, when I plant in October I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — that is the 15-15-15 kind, about 50 kg per mu. Then in March, when the wheat starts jointing, I spread another 20 kg of urea per mu. I know that is a solid amount because two years ago I tried to save money and only used 15 kg of urea, and the wheat turned yellow. I lost yield. A bad harvest is a disaster for me — I live alone, I cannot afford that. Wasting a little fertilizer is just a cost I can absorb. I will irrigate twice from my well: once before winter so the wheat can survive the cold, and once at jointing in spring. I used to irrigate three times, but pumping water is hard work now that I am alone and my back is not good. Twice is what I can manage. I spray twice: once for weeds after the wheat comes up, and once for insects when it heads. I hire the neighbor's rotary tiller before sowing because I cannot turn the soil myself anymore. It costs me, but I have no choice. If the weather is normal, I expect about 450 kg per mu.

For my summer maize: As soon as the wheat is out in June, I plant hybrid maize. Everyone uses hybrid seed now — the old traditional seed disappeared years ago. I use about 2.5 kg of seed per mu. At planting I put down 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu, the same 15-15-15 kind. Then when the maize reaches the big trumpet stage, I add 25 kg of urea per mu. That is what my neighbors do. I irrigate once, at tasseling time in July or August. Summer maize gets some rain, but that one irrigation is what fills the ears. Without it, you get empty tips. I spray twice: herbicide before the maize emerges, and then once for corn borers if I see them in the field. For tillage, I do not plow deep for maize — I plant into the wheat stubble to save time and labor. I expect about 550 kg per mu if the rain cooperates.

I think about my whole budget. I am one person on 4.1 mu. Every bag of fertilizer is real money out of my pocket. But I have learned over 40 years that on a small plot like mine, trying to save on inputs usually costs you more at harvest. I would rather put down a bit too much than risk losing yield. I copy what the successful farmers around me do. That is how I decide.
